messages:
alex: Heads up — starting ~09:20 UTC we're seeing token-stream stalls and gRPC stream resets for streaming inference in us-west-2 (primarily AZ-b -> AZ-c east-west paths). 95p token-latency jumped ~80ms -> ~1.8s and stream reset rate up ~8x.

infra-bot: :warning: alert: packet-reordering anomalies detected in cluster us-west-2 (metric: packet_reorder_rate) — threshold breached at 09:19:58 UTC

priya: Which fleets/models are hitting this? Batches or streaming-only?

alex: Streaming-heavy fleets (gpt-13k and gpt-chat-prod). Non-streaming RPC latency looks mostly fine. Batches that rely on long-lived streams to push tokens are getting tail stalls (tokens arrive in bursts then silence).

jamie: Can you paste `ethtool -S` and `tc qdisc show` from affected hosts? Also confirm whether RDMA/roce traffic shares NICs with host networking.

alex: Quick dumps from one host (trimmed):
```
$ ethtool -S eth0 | egrep 'reorder|drop|miss'
rx_dropped: 12
rx_missed: 0
rx_nohandler: 0
rx_packets_reordered: 147
tx_packets_reordered: 132

$ tc qdisc show dev eth0
qdisc fq_codel 0: root refcnt 2 limit 10240p flows 1024 quantum 1514 target 5.0ms interval 100.0ms
backlog 2500p requeues 3
```
(note: vendor counters include `rx_packets_reordered`)

priya: That `rx_packets_reordered` is telling. Any MTU mismatch between host and switch? Also, are GRO/GSO/TSO enabled?

alex: Host MTU 9000, switch on-path shows 9216 on some leafs (we're chasing a fabric config drift from last week). GRO/GSO enabled by default.

jamie: MTU mismatch + aggressive GRO/GSO can cause out-of-order seen by application TCP stacks for streaming workloads (small packets followed by coalesced ones). Also, bursts can reorder on multi-path ECMP if hash keys change due to source port churn.

ops-jen: @alex can you run `sudo ethtool -k eth0 | egrep 'gro|gso|tso'` and `sudo sysctl net.core.rmem_max net.core.netdev_max_backlog` on one of the hosts? We'll run iperf and ibv tests for RDMA.

alex: Results:
```
$ ethtool -k eth0 | egrep 'gro|gso|tso'
rx-gro: on
tx-gso: on
tso: on

$ sysctl net.core.rmem_max net.core.netdev_max_backlog
net.core.rmem_max = 212992
net.core.netdev_max_backlog = 1000
```

alex: Ran `iperf3 -c peer -P 8` between AZ-b/hostA -> AZ-c/hostB, saw occasional reordering/packet arrival jitter and throughput briefly drop then recover. RDMA checks (`ibv_rc_pingpong`) show more stable latency but we have mixed workloads using RoCE and UDP paths.

priya: Immediate mitigation options: 1) enforce MTU consistency (set 9000 everywhere or drop to 1500 temporarily) 2) disable GRO/GSO on affected NICs to avoid coalescing-induced reorder (cpu hit) 3) increase `net.core.netdev_max_backlog` and `rmem_max` to absorb bursts 4) bump streaming RPC deadlines and enable token-batching fallback to avoid aborts.

jamie: Short-term I'd prefer disabling GRO on the serving hosts in the affected AZ pair to see if reorder counters fall and stream stalls reduce. That is reversible. Also pinning pod->host (AZ-local routing) to avoid cross-AZ ECMP for heavy-streaming flows while we root-cause.

ops-jen: Ops privilege: I can flip GRO/GSO on a small canary pool in AZ-b now and route one fleet there. Schedule?

alex: Please canary on 3 hosts, route 5% of gpt-chat-prod streaming traffic. I'll monitor token latency dashboards.

ops-jen: Doing canary now (09:46 UTC). Command: `sudo ethtool -K eth0 gro off gso off tso off` on host{a,b,c}.

infra-bot: change: hostA (id i-0abc) GRO/GSO/TPO toggled by ops-jen at 09:46:12 UTC

alex: Early numbers: 95p token latency down from 1.8s -> 220ms on canary hosts, stream resets near zero for canary. Reorder counters dropped to single digits.

priya: Good sign. Next: plan a short maintenance to roll the change across the AZ pair and coordinate with network team to fix MTU mismatch. Also check switch firmware — last upgrade had asymmetric behavior on ECMP.

jamie: Longer term: 1) reconcile MTU across fabric, 2) vendor patch / NIC firmware update to address reordering at high line rates, 3) consider dedicating RDMA fabrics for RoCE traffic and isolating TCP streaming on separate NICs or VLANs, 4) add a runtime knob to reduce stream window sizes (so TCP retransmission/backoff less likely to reorder tokens).

alex: Cost implication: If we keep disabling GRO/GSO permanently we'll increase CPU usage ~6-10% on serving hosts — that reduces effective GPU throughput and would require ~20% more GPU fleet to maintain capacity (~$Xk/month). We'll track before committing to permanent change.

ops-jen: Network team scheduled MTU reconciliation for tonight 02:00 UTC PST (maintenance window). NIC firmware upgrade tentatively next week. I'll open a follow-up ticket and link here.

alex: Filing follow-up: https://redwood-inc.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-8274 — includes logs, ethtool dumps, iperf results, and canary metrics.

priya: Also rolling a runtime fallback: if stream token gaps exceed 300ms we will switch to short-polling fallback for that session and increase RPC deadline by 500ms. Deploying a canary to 5% today.

jamie: Thanks everyone. Once MTU & firmware are fixed, we'll re-evaluate turning GRO/GSO back on and measure CPU/GPU delta.

alex: Current status: canary looks stable at 10:12 UTC — reduced reorder metrics, streaming tails improved. Leaving thread open until MTU reconciliation and firmware done. :thumbsup:
